title: Kodiak and IKEA: Launching Driverless Service in 2026 After Four Years of Partnership
summary: After four years, 1,300+ loads and 750,000 autonomous miles together, IKEA will be Kodiak's driverless launch partner on a 219-mile I-45 route in Texas.
body_markdown:
# Kodiak and IKEA: Launching Driverless Service in 2026 After Four Years of Partnership


[Don Burnette](https://kodiak.ai/news?author=don-burnette)


|


September 29, 2026


For four years, Kodiak and IKEA Supply have built a blueprint for reshaping freight transportation with autonomous driving technology. Soon, we’re embarking on the next step of this ambitious partnership.


IKEA will be Kodiak’s driverless launch shipper partner later in 2026, and become the first company to take advantage of the safety and efficiency benefits that result from Kodiak’s driverless freight capabilities.


This has already been an incredible collaboration. Over the last four years, Kodiak has delivered more than 1,300 loads and logged more than 750,000 miles while autonomously carrying IKEA goods with a safety observer aboard.


We have delivered great service seven days a week, night and day, rain and shine, with an impressive, nearly perfect on-time delivery record.


Together, we’ve grown to understand how autonomous driving technology can improve safety and enhance reliability throughout the IKEA supply chain. We now know exactly what it takes to transform the underlying technology into an AI-driven product that generates value and efficiency.


Unsupervised driverless operations – no human in the cab – represent a milestone the entire Kodiak team has been tirelessly working toward since Kodiak was founded more than eight years ago. We are now only months away, and we could not be more excited to have IKEA as our partner on this journey.


**Initial driver-out service focused on I-45 in Texas**


Just as IKEA built a global business providing well-designed, functional home furnishings at affordable prices, our work together has forged the capabilities and know-how needed for a well-designed, cost-effective driverless product our customers can efficiently utilize and rely upon.


Service will begin on the same route we’ve safely tested in Texas for four years without incident.


The initial driver-out leg will cover 219 miles, primarily along Interstate 45 between Kodiak’s Houston and Dallas-area facilities. This is part of the established 292-mile delivery route connecting the IKEA distribution center in Baytown with the IKEA store in Frisco.


In preparation for this service, we have learned not only the big things but also the little things that really matter: Exactly when and where trucks should be launched; Knowing precisely what time they will arrive in Frisco so unloading can be scheduled at a specific dock door; Collecting predictive maintenance data insights and establishing proactive maintenance plans for trucks.


This orchestration allows for greater asset utilization and improved reliability throughout the supply chain.


**Safety commitment drives everything we do**


We know the big things matter too: Safety underpins everything.


Ahead of our launch, Kodiak is completing our highway launch safety case for driverless long-haul operations. Our safety case is a structured, evidence-backed argument that the Kodiak Driver, our autonomous driving system, is safe to operate without a human on board in a defined operating area.


By concentrating on long-haul routes, Kodiak and IKEA have learned how adopting autonomous truck technology can enhance human driver’s quality of life, focusing their efforts on the local driving jobs that most prefer. They can reduce their time sleeping on the side of the highway and instead be home with family and friends.


**Road ahead includes building trust, gaining traction**


While the driver-out milestone marks a proud moment, it is worth remembering it is just a moment, this is another exciting and important step in our now four-year journey together and the journey to come.


This is not a one-off endeavor. Our work scaling driverless technology throughout freight transportation will continue with IKEA and others after this upcoming launch. Mile by mile, we intend to build trust and gain traction until driver-out service is a routine and everyday part of the long-haul trucking landscape.


For now, Kodiak is undergoing its final checks in preparation for this landmark moment – those include learning how to pronounce “FÖRARLÖS LASTBIL.” That is “driverless truck” in Swedish!
